questions.question: In casting terminology, the 'pattern' is:

options.A: A replica of the object to be cast, used to form the mould cavity

questions.question: The 'core' in casting is used to:

options.A: Produce internal cavities/hollow features in the casting

questions.question: 'Chaplets' are used in casting to:

options.A: Support cores inside the mould cavity and prevent core shift
options.B: Feed molten metal into the mould
options.D: Remove the pattern from the sand

questions.question: The 'draft' or taper given to a pattern refers to:

options.A: A slight taper provided on vertical faces for easy pattern withdrawal

questions.question: 'Parting line' in mould making refers to:

options.A: The line/plane separating the cope and drag halves of the mould
options.B: The line where the metal solidifies last

questions.question: 'Cope' and 'drag' refer to:

options.A: The upper and lower halves of a sand mould, respectively

questions.question: Pattern allowances typically include all of the following EXCEPT:

options.A: Shrinkage allowance

questions.question: A cast-iron casting requires a linear dimension of 200 mm after machining. If the machining allowance is 3 mm and the shrinkage allowance is 1%, the pattern dimension is approximately:
A green sand mould is composed primarily of:

options.A: Silica sand, clay (bentonite) and moisture

questions.question: The term 'green' in green sand moulding refers to:

options.A: The sand being moist/undried (not baked), not its colour

questions.question: The clay commonly used as a binder in green sand moulding is:

options.A: Bentonite

questions.question: A typical limitation of green sand moulding is:

options.A: Lower dimensional accuracy and surface finish compared to shell/investment casting
options.C: Very high mould cost for every casting

questions.question: Permeability of a green sand mould refers to its ability to:

options.A: Allow gases/steam generated during pouring to escape through the mould

questions.question: Excessive moisture content in green sand is most likely to cause:

options.A: Blowholes/gas porosity due to steam generation

questions.question: Green sand mould strength (green compressive strength) is primarily influenced by:

options.A: Clay content, moisture content and degree of ramming

questions.question: Advantages of green sand moulding include:

options.A: Low cost, reusability of sand, and suitability for a wide range of casting sizes
options.B: Dimensional accuracy comparable to investment casting

questions.question: Investment casting is also known as:

options.A: Lost-wax casting

questions.question: In investment casting, the pattern is typically made of:

options.A: Wax (or a similar expendable material)

questions.question: Investment casting is well suited for producing:

options.A: Intricate, high-precision, thin-walled components with excellent surface finish
options.C: Only components requiring a permanent metallic mould

questions.question: In die casting, the mould (die) is:

options.A: A reusable, permanent metal mould

questions.question: Die casting is generally used for casting:

options.A: Low-melting-point non-ferrous metals such as aluminium, zinc and magnesium alloys

questions.question: The two main types of die casting processes are:

options.A: Hot chamber and cold chamber die casting
options.C: Green sand and dry sand casting

questions.question: Hot chamber die casting is generally preferred for:

options.A: Low-melting-point metals like zinc that do not readily attack the injection system

questions.question: Cold chamber die casting is generally used for:

options.A: Metals like aluminium with higher melting points that would corrode a hot-chamber injection system

questions.question: A key advantage of die casting is:

options.A: High production rate with excellent dimensional accuracy and surface finish for mass production
options.B: Suitability for very high melting point metals

questions.question: A limitation of investment casting compared to sand casting is:

options.A: Higher cost and generally limited to smaller-sized components

questions.question: The pattern material selected depends on factors such as:

options.A: Number of castings required, dimensional accuracy needed, and complexity of shape
options.B: Only the cost of the metal being cast
options.C: Only the colour of the final casting

questions.question: Common pattern materials include:

options.A: Wood, metal, plastic and wax

questions.question: A 'split pattern' is used when:

options.A: The casting shape makes it impossible to withdraw a single-piece pattern from the mould
options.B: Only a single casting is required

questions.question: A 'match-plate pattern' is characterised by:

options.A: Cope and drag pattern halves mounted on opposite sides of a single plate
options.B: A pattern made entirely of wax
options.C: A pattern with no parting line
options.D: A one-piece solid pattern with no cope/drag distinction

questions.question: Core sand generally requires higher strength than mould sand because:

options.A: Cores are surrounded by molten metal on most sides and subjected to greater thermal/metallostatic forces
options.C: Core sand is always compacted less
options.D: Cores do not need to resist gas pressure

questions.question: 'Core prints' are:

options.A: Extensions on the pattern that form seats to support and locate the core in the mould
options.B: The printed marking on the final casting
options.D: The gating channel passing through the core

questions.question: Core venting is important because it:

options.A: Allows gases generated within the core during pouring to escape, preventing defects
options.D: Has no effect on casting quality

questions.question: Which of the following is generally NOT used as a core sand binder?

options.A: Oil (as in oil-sand cores)
options.C: Bentonite clay (mainly used in mould sand, not core sand)

questions.question: Solidification of a pure metal in a mould begins:

options.A: At the mould wall, where nucleation and heat extraction are highest
options.B: At the geometric centre of the casting

questions.question: Chvorinov's rule relates the solidification time of a casting to:

options.A: Its (Volume/Surface area) ratio, i.e., t = C(V/A)ⁿ

questions.question: If the (Volume/Surface area) ratio of casting A is twice that of casting B (same mould, n = 2), the solidification time of A relative to B is:

options.A: 4 times

questions.question: Directional solidification in casting is achieved to ensure:

options.A: Progressive solidification from the farthest point toward the riser, so liquid metal is always available to feed shrinkage
options.B: Uniform solidification throughout at the same instant
options.C: Solidification starts at the riser first
options.D: No feeding of shrinkage is needed

questions.question: Chills are placed in a mould primarily to:

options.A: Locally increase the cooling rate and promote directional solidification
options.C: Insulate the mould and slow cooling everywhere
options.D: Completely replace risers in all cases

questions.question: Which zone is NOT typically observed in the solidified structure of a casting?

options.A: Chill zone (fine equiaxed grains near the mould wall)
options.D: A single uniform grain zone throughout

questions.question: Shrinkage in castings occurs in three stages — liquid shrinkage, solidification shrinkage, and:

options.A: Solid-state (patternmaker's) shrinkage as the solid cools to room temperature

questions.question: A riser is primarily designed to compensate for which stage(s) of shrinkage?

options.A: Liquid shrinkage and solidification shrinkage

questions.question: The main functions of a gating system include:

options.A: Delivering molten metal to the mould cavity while minimising turbulence, oxidation and erosion

questions.question: The components of a gating system, in typical order of metal flow, are:

options.A: Pouring basin → sprue → runner → gate → mould cavity
options.D: Mould cavity → gate → sprue → pouring basin

questions.question: A tapered sprue (decreasing cross-section from top to bottom) is used to:

options.A: Prevent aspiration/air entrainment as flow velocity increases downward
options.D: Reduce metal velocity as it descends

questions.question: Using Bernoulli's equation, if molten metal falls through a sprue height of 0.2 m (neglecting losses, g = 9.81 m/s²), the velocity at the sprue exit is approximately:
A gating ratio of 1 : 2 : 2 (sprue : runner : gate, by cross-sectional area) is an example of:

options.A: A non-pressurised gating system
options.C: A gating system with no runner
options.D: A bottom gating system without a sprue

questions.question: In a pressurised gating system, the total gate area is generally:

options.A: Smaller than or equal to the runner area, maintaining backpressure to reduce turbulence at the gate
options.B: Much larger than the sprue area

questions.question: Bottom gating (uphill gating) is preferred over top gating for many alloys mainly because it:

options.A: Reduces turbulence and metal splashing/oxidation during mould filling
options.D: Eliminates the need for a riser

questions.question: A 'skim gate' or 'whirl gate' in the gating system is primarily used to:

options.A: Trap slag/dross and prevent it from entering the mould cavity
options.D: Speed up solidification of the gate itself

questions.question: The main function of a riser in casting is to:

options.A: Act as a reservoir of molten metal to compensate for solidification shrinkage

questions.question: For a riser to be effective, it must solidify:

options.A: After the casting section it is feeding (i.e., last to solidify)
options.B: Before the casting section it is feeding
options.C: At exactly the same time as the casting
options.D: Timing of riser solidification is irrelevant

questions.question: According to Chvorinov's rule, to ensure a riser solidifies later than the casting, the riser's (Volume/Surface area) ratio should be:

options.A: Greater than that of the casting
options.B: Less than that of the casting
options.C: Equal to that of the casting

questions.question: A cylindrical riser is generally more metal-efficient than which shape, owing to a lower surface-area-to-volume ratio for a given volume?

options.A: A thin plate/slab-shaped riser
options.C: Shape has no bearing on efficiency
options.D: A cubical riser, which is always most efficient

questions.question: 'Riser yield' is defined as:

options.A: Ratio of casting weight to (casting weight + riser weight), expressed as a percentage
options.B: Ratio of riser weight to casting weight only
options.C: The tensile strength of the riser metal
options.D: The number of risers used per mould

questions.question: Open risers (open to the atmosphere) compared to blind risers primarily differ in that open risers:

options.A: Allow visual inspection and easier gas escape, but may lose heat faster
options.B: Are completely enclosed within the mould, invisible from outside
options.C: Cannot be used for feeding shrinkage
options.D: Are never used in green sand moulds

questions.question: 'Blowholes' in a casting are caused primarily by:

options.A: Entrapped gas that could not escape the mould during solidification

questions.question: 'Shrinkage cavity' defects occur when:

options.A: Adequate directional solidification/feeding via risers is not provided, leaving voids in the last-to-solidify region
options.C: The pouring temperature is too low

questions.question: A 'cold shut' defect occurs when:

options.A: Two streams of molten metal meet without fusing completely, often due to low pouring temperature or slow filling

questions.question: 'Sand inclusion'/dross defects in castings are primarily caused by:

options.A: Loose sand or slag particles carried into the mould cavity along with the molten metal
